[chunk 3/4] Extracted from Alphabet 10-Q (GOOGL, filed 2025-07-24). Key SIFI-material findings: (1) Wiz acquisition ($32B cash, pending 2026 close) signals Google Cloud aggressive capex deployment amid ongoing antitrust scrutiny. (2) Capex ROI gap: Alphabet deployed $44.8B capex in H1 2025 (annualizes ~$90B), driven by "technical infrastructure" investments for AI/cloud, while Google Cloud revenues are only $25.9B in H1 with operating income $5B—capex growth vastly outpaces revenue growth, signaling execution risk and potential stranded assets if AI cloud market slows or regulatory remedies constrain distribution. (3) Multi-front antitrust exposure: Search (DOJ ruling + remedies decision expected Aug 2025), AdTech (publisher tools violation + remedies Sept 2025), Google Play (Epic verdict + remedies already issued, appeal in progress), Android (EC/Japan JFTC orders). Severity 4 risks on Search and AdTech due to "structural remedies" language and material adverse effect warnings. (4) Privacy settlement $1.4B in April 2025 (Severity 2). No PE portfolio or AILab investments named in this excerpt; Wiz is a cloud security platform, not an AI lab. Generic APT/China risks and routine competition skipped per guidelines.
[chunk 4/4] SIFI MATERIAL FINDINGS:

1. **CAPEX INTENSITY WITHOUT EXPLICIT AI CIRCULARITY**: Alphabet increased capex from $25.2B (H1 2024) to $39.6B (H1 2025)—a 57% YoY jump. The filing explicitly states "We expect to increase, relative to 2024, our investment in our technical infrastructure, including servers, network equipment, and data centers, to support the growth of our business and our long-term initiatives, in particular in support of AI products and services." This is a CAPEX_ROI_GAP signal: massive infrastructure spend explicitly tied to AI, but no disclosed AI customer revenue split, no AI-specific SLAs, no named AI lab contractual commitments visible in this 10-Q excerpt. The risk is execution: "Assets not yet in service are those that are not ready for our intended use... data center construction projects are generally multi-year projects."

2. **FUTURE LEASE OBLIGATIONS OFF-BALANCE**: As of June 30, 2025, Alphabet has "entered into leases primarily related to data centers that have not yet commenced with future lease payments of $23.9 billion. These leases will commence between 2025 and 2031 with non-cancelable lease terms between one and 25 years." This is a HIDDEN_LEVERAGE signal: $23.9B in committed future data center lease obligations are not reflected on the balance sheet yet, only disclosed in Note 4. Combined with the $39.6B capex burn and vague AI ROI justification, this creates execution and depreciation-life risk.

3. **WIZ ACQUISITION ($32B)**: A pending all-cash acquisition for a cloud security platform, signed March 2025, expected to close in 2026 "subject to customary closing conditions, including the receipt of regulatory approvals." While strategically sound (cloud security for Google Cloud), this is a SIFI material capital allocation event: $32B in liquidity tied up pending regulatory approval—adds financial flexibility risk if approval is delayed or denied.

4. **GENERIC RISK REFERENCES**: The filing states "For details on risks related to our manufacturing and supply chain and other risks, refer to Part I, Item 1A, 'Risk Factors' in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2024." This excerpt does NOT include Item 1A details, so no named counterparty concentration or supplier single-source risks are visible here.

5. **NO AI LAB INVESTMENTS, NO CIRCULAR EXPOSURE**: This excerpt makes no reference to investments in OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, or other private AI labs—no equity stakes disclosed. The Wiz deal is purely acquisition (cloud security), not circularity.

6. **MATERIAL PURCHASE COMMITMENTS ($72.5B)**: Alphabet discloses "material purchase commitments and other contractual obligations of $72.5 billion, of which $51.0 billion was short-term. These amounts primarily consist of purchase orders for certain technical infrastructure as well as the non-cancelable portion or the minimum cancellation fee in certain agreements related to commitments to purchase licenses, including content licenses, inventory, and network capacity." This is substantial operating leverage, but composition is opaque—no breakdown by supplier, no single-supplier concentration metric provided.

7. **TAC DEPENDENCE**: Google Network and Search properties are heavily dependent on traffic acquisition cost (TAC) to distribution partners; TAC rate of 20.6% on $186.7B H1 2025 revenue = ~$38.4B annual TAC burn. Not a counterparty concentration risk (distributed across many partners), but indicates margin vulnerability if TAC rates rise.
